directChecks.check: 33 analog, feedback, compensation and ADC trace geometries
directChecks.method: Exact exported wire endpoints; Euclidean planar lengths; route wire-to-wire adjacent equal-layer segments only; via counts exclude external via components; foreign trace capsule edge distance by independent segment distance. This check excludes pads, pours, via annuli and ground traces.

directChecks.check: Selected sensitive traces versus all foreign non-ground trace capsules on the same layer
Shunt terminals and four dedicated pickup endpoint identities
directChecks.evidence: TEC_SENSE_KELVIN_P and TEC_MON_KELVIN_P start on pcb_port_187 at (25.645,12); N branches start on pcb_port_188 at (31.355,12). Separate 0.2 mm pickups exit toward the inner shunt land edges; main shunt pad dimensions are 1.65 x 3.68 mm.
pcb_copper_pour_0 is GND on inner1 with 164 voids; ground pours exist on bottom and locally on top. No GND copper pour exists on inner2 in the reviewed export.

strengths: Controller and independent INA219 telemetry have separate, explicit narrow pickups from the actual R20 lands rather than remote taps on power copper.

The raw controller Kelvin pair runs together for 20.9 mm on bottom, with 0.5 mm center spacing and 0.3 mm copper edge spacing. Paired routing is present where the long horizontal trunk passes the power section.
The current filters are beside the controller and beside the shunt monitor. Measured monitor capacitor-to-resistor traces are 2.05 and 3.44 mm.
Voltage feedback and output telemetry sample the post-shunt output capacitor C29 instead of the switch or inductor node.
ADC probes connect downstream of their RC filters, and the fan power branch is distinct from the low-current input-voltage ADC tap.
Independent selected-trace checks found no foreign non-ground trace overlap; connectivity/lint success alone was not used as the score.

findings.explanation: The regulator current-sense path remains long and incompletely paired at its ends. The two raw paths are 34.33 and 36.73 mm and use two vias each. The long middle section is well paired, but the pickups and controller-end bends separate. This increases differential loop exposure relative to a shorter, continuously paired Kelvin path; no quantified current-regulation error is established by static geometry. Length matching for propagation delay is not the concern.

After the sense RC filter, the positive controller leg is 3.885 mm on top with zero vias, whereas the negative leg is 6.23 mm and changes to bottom and back through two vias. Different routing and layer environments can convert common-mode pickup into differential error. The magnitude is unmeasured, so this is a targeted improvement recommendation rather than a proved malfunction.

The sensitive VC compensation network is spread away from the controller. U2 VC to R27 is 15.186 mm planar across three pieces, then R27 to C33 is 5.088 mm; C33 has a further 6.196 mm top ground escape to its return via. Ground continuity does not erase the added lead geometry. Moving R27/C33 and the return nearer VC/controller ground would reduce parasitic coupling and improve layout economy. This is an inferred sensitivity concern, with no demonstrated stability failure.

Bottom Kelvin and selected bottom ADC routes do not have an adjacent dedicated ground plane because inner2 carries routed signals. A broad ground plane does exist on inner1. This does not prove excessive noise, but the quiet routes should be checked against the actual four-layer dielectric stack and nearby aggressors before regarding their return environment as optimal.
findings.evidence: Actual copper pour inventory: GND pours on inner1, bottom and local top; no inner2 GND pour. Bottom Kelvin trunk geometries recorded in measurements JSON.

findings.explanation: Main feedback divider to U2 is 9.727 mm planar with two external transfer vias, and the fan feedback divider/compensation local legs are each approximately 6.4 mm for endpoints less than 3 mm apart. Both are candidates for shorter placement-led routing. The 33.27 mm main output pickup is on the low-impedance output side of the divider and therefore should not be conflated with the sensitive feedback node.

suspectedShortAssessment.status: No confirmed short found in this analog trace subset; user crop not independently localized in this role.
suspectedShortAssessment.evidence: Independent same-layer foreign non-ground trace capsule tests for 33 named traces: zero overlaps and minimum positive copper edge gap 0.224264 mm. This does not check every pad, pour, via annulus, ground trace or the screenshot region and must not be promoted to a whole-board no-short certificate.

topImprovements: Place R27/C33 near U2 VC, with a short capacitor return to controller ground; this is the largest avoidable sensitive-node detour in the reviewed analog area.
Route both post-filter SENSE legs together on one layer with the same layer transitions; shorten the negative bottom excursion.
Keep raw Kelvin pair spacing controlled through the pickup and receiver bends, not only through its long central trunk.
Move both feedback divider groups closer to their controller pins and shorten the fan local loops.
Validate the resulting quiet route reference geometry against the actual fabrication dielectric stack and current-switch aggressor paths.
limitations: No source or PCB changes, rerouting, builds or fabrication exports were performed.
The score judges this exact exported static geometry from an analog perspective; it does not deduct merely because hardware is unbuilt.
The dedicated independent clearance calculation excludes pads, pours, via annuli and ground traces; it cannot certify the entire PCB against shorts.
Noise susceptibility and stability effects are explicitly inferred from geometry. No electromagnetic, transient, loop-gain or bench measurements were performed.
Lengths are planar trace lengths and exclude physical barrel depth; inline via counts do not include separate explicitly declared transfer via components.
